column1: # The wire's own bytes, for anyone implementing a receiver or a server
# (DOC-1963, DEC-1759 lesson 3). The engine and the server run
# every row; the engine keeps an exact copy of this file, which its commit
# gate compares, as `neoteletext_web::wire_vectors::TABLE`, and the server
# reads that copy, as both read the address map's table.
# Four columns, separated by tabs: kind, name, value, meaning.
# version  value is what both sides must say; meaning says where.
# close    value is a close code; meaning is what a receiver does.
# input    value is one message of the input stream, in hexadecimal; meaning
#          is the item it reads as. It writes back to the same bytes unless
#          the name begins `skipped`, and a server told it does as meaning says.
# refused  value is a message a reader must refuse at the top level of the
#          stream: a protocol error, closed with close code 4000 (DOC-1919).
#          Under push protocol 10 that includes a well-formed event of the
#          viewer's input, which may stand only inside a RULE_EVENT
# record   value is one 42-byte packet 4/31 on data channel 12, service 0,
#          record id as meaning says, in hexadecimal; meaning is the record.
# The rows below those are the page rule table's and animation's, in the
# table's second form at push protocol 10 (docs/page-rules.md RULE-85,
# docs/animation.md ANIM-23). The engine writes them with
# `cargo xtask wire-vectors`, and its tests hold that this table has what
# that prints; they are never typed by hand. Every one is for page 101,
# rules       value is the image of one page's table, in hexadecimal
#             (RULE-41): a header of twelve bytes, then its rectangles,
#             rows, rules, groups and sequences. It holds neither its page
#             nor its sub-code, which the RULES record that carries it
#             does. It decodes for page 101/0001, and encodes back to the
# command     value is the body of one command, in hexadecimal: the bytes a
#             record of that type carries and the bytes a group holds
#             (RULE-45). The name begins with the record: variable (type
#             29, RULE-99, each operation with each operand kind), report
#             regis_cursor (16). It reads, and writes back to the same
# rule_event  value is one message of the input stream, a RULE_EVENT
#             (RULE-46); it reads, and writes back to the same bytes.
# records     value is the packets 4/31 of one record, each 42 bytes in
#             hexadecimal, fragment 0 first, separated by one space; service
#             0, record id 0. The name begins with the record: rules (type
# object      value is one whole OBJECT record of the audio profile as it is
#             framed, before it is cut into fragments: version, type, a
#             two-byte body length, the body and a CRC-32 (RULE-60).
# and their `records` rows `rules_rule_35` to `rules_music_player`, are the
# images of RULE-35's example, page-rules.md's worked examples of section
# 7.5 and the music player's table of RULE-93, each moved to page 101/0001,
# and the RULES record each travels in at generation 1. The server writes
# them, since it turns their names into numbers (neoteletext-app-server's
# protocol tests, whose copy of these rows its check script holds equal to
# this file's); the engine's tests hold each image to decode for page
# 101/0001 and to encode back to the same bytes.
# The `object` row `local_sound_as_the_server_writes_it` is the same sound as
# `local_sound` with the variant's tag (5, one byte, 0: synth106) before the
# banks' tag, as the server writes every sound of the synth106 and synth53
# families: three bytes more, and the same sound to a reader.
# Renderer parity (docs/renderer-parity.md PAR-44) adds rows the engine
# writes with the same command, for page 101, sub-code 0001:
# - `input hello_pictures` and `record welcome_pictures`: HELLO offering, and
#   WELCOME agreeing, REGIS_CAP (bit 23) and NAPLPS_CAP (bit 24) with the
#   (type 15) and REGIS_CURSOR (type 16) for a NAPLPS sub-page, naming its
#   object 301. Their bytes are those for a ReGIS sub-page naming drawing
#   301: which the number names is the sub-page's picture language (PAR-2).
#   program messages regis_links, naplps_links, regis_cursor and
#   naplps_cursor as a rule table's group holds them, the links one whole
#   table whose rule `open` runs a group holding a NAPLPS picture's links
#   and cursor, as the server writes {"groups":[{"name":"links","commands":
# picture_text  value is the bytes the engine's picture text encoder writes
#               for one text part (PAR-3 to PAR-5), in hexadecimal: the name
#               begins `regis` or `naplps`, the picture language, and the
#               meaning is the part as a program gives it in a `regis` or
#               A server given that part writes those bytes.
